problem: Traditional mobile-robot navigation stacks chain many small localization, perception, prediction, planning and control modules. They depend on artificial landmarks (QR codes) in repetitive indoor scenes, and VPR-style retrieval loses fine detail and cannot output pose. Learned end-to-end planners still collide often.
motivation: General-purpose indoor robots (warehouse, office, home) need to understand language goals, localize in repetitive environments without artificial markers, and avoid obstacles in real time. The paper follows a System 1/System 2 split: a slow, semantic MLLM for global reasoning and a fast multi-task network for local control.
key_idea: A dual-model hierarchy: Astra-Global, an MLLM (Qwen2.5-VL, SFT+GRPO) over a topological-semantic landmark map for goal and self-localization, and Astra-Local, a self-supervised 4D spatial-temporal encoder with a flow-matching planning head (masked ESDF loss) and a multi-sensor transformer odometry head.
insight: RL (GRPO) after SFT improves zero-shot generalization and sample efficiency: SFT+GRPO with 100k+20k samples reaches 99.9% on the unseen Home scene versus 93.7% for SFT-only with 100k and 97.3% with 300k. Adding the 4D forecasting encoder over a 3D-only encoder lowers OOD collision rate (FM+ESDF 10.3% to 8.0%) and raises velocity. Odometry accuracy comes from temporal and multi-sensor fusion: RTE goes 5.46% (BEV-ODOM) to 3.13% (visual only) to 2.04% (+IMU) to 1.92% (+wheel).
method: Offline hybrid topological-semantic map: SfM (COLMAP) on a demo tour video gives keyframe nodes with 6-DoF poses and pose-based edges. Astra-Global annotates landmarks (category, visual attributes, functional description) and builds a landmark-node co-visibility registry.

Astra-Global coarse-to-fine localization: the coarse stage detects landmarks in the query and matches them to map landmarks, then applies visual co-visibility filtering to get candidate nodes. The fine stage takes the query plus nearby reference nodes (image+pose) and directly outputs the query pose. Goal localization matches text to landmark functional descriptions, searching near the current location first.

Astra-Global training: Qwen2.5-VL backbone, SFT on coarse/fine localization plus auxiliary tasks (co-visibility detection, co-visible image selection, movement trend), then GRPO with rule-based rewards (format, landmark recall, map-ID IoU, extra-landmark pose reward; co-visibility score reward).
3D spatial encoder: ViT plus lift-splat-shoot to voxel features, self-supervised via SDF/color volumetric rendering against DepthAnything-V2 pseudo-depth (RANSAC-aligned to sensor depth).

4D spatial-temporal encoder: forecasts future voxel features from past frames and future timestamps using a 3D-conv ResNet, DiT blocks per level and an FPN3D, trained with voxel-level plus rendered depth/color losses.

Planning head: transformer conditional flow matching on trajectories of (dx, dy, dtheta), conditioned on voxel features, occupancy, velocity and goal. A masked ESDF loss (ESDF masked by an expanded GT-trajectory region) is added at training time, with no extra inference cost.

Odometry head: transformer over modality tokens (BEV-correlation of 4D vision features, LSTM-encoded IMU and wheel data) across the current and previous 9 frames, with a CLS token regressing relative pose under L1 loss.

setting.backbone: Astra-Global: Qwen2.5-VL (fine-tuned with SFT+GRPO); Astra-Local: ViT-S/ViT-L 3D encoder + DiT 4D encoder + transformer flow-matching planner + transformer odometry head (trained from scratch)
setting.model_size: Astra-Global size not stated; Astra-Local encoder ViT-S/ViT-L, planner Small/Medium/Large
setting.training_data: Astra-Global: in-house warehouse and office image-pose data; 100k-300k SFT samples plus 20k-200k GRPO samples; home scenes held out for zero-shot. Astra-Local: ~10M self-supervised encoder samples (in-house plus open-source), 10M human-teleoperated trajectory samples for the planner, in-house multi-modal odometry data.
setting.observation: Multi-camera RGB (tri-camera), IMU, wheel odometry; single-frame RGB for global localization; text instruction
setting.action_space: Local trajectory waypoints (dx, dy, dtheta) for a wheeled robot, with a rule-based optimization-planner fallback
setting.simulator: real world only (in-house data and robots)
setting.privileged: Pre-built map from a demonstration tour video (pre-exploration) is used; no other privileged information

numbers_note: No standard benchmark is used. Results are on in-house warehouse, office and home data, so nothing maps to a canonical benchmark. Many results appear only in figures (e.g. the VPR comparison in Fig. 'compare_with_vpr'). Key in-house numbers: end-to-end SR 84.2% (warehouse) and 99.1% (office); goal localization SR 98.3% and 99.1%; self-localization SR 85.9% and 100%; fallback rate 8.3% and 15.6%.
results: On in-house robots, Astra reaches end-to-end mission SR of 84.2% (warehouse) and 99.1% (office). Astra-Global beats MixVPR in all scenes, and in the zero-shot home scene gets 81.8% vs 57.7% at 1m/5° (91.1% after fine-tuning). Astra-Local beats BEV-ODOM on odometry (RTE 1.92% vs 5.46%) and beats OccWorld and Cam4DOcc on occupancy forecasting (Obstacle IoU 56.66 vs 51.01). The masked ESDF loss lowers collision rates, and flow matching outperforms ACT and diffusion policy.
limitations: Astra-Global localizes from single frames and fails in featureless or highly repetitive spots (warehouse start-point failures; end-to-end SR rises to 91.2% when these are excluded). The map compression may also drop semantic detail.
Astra-Local has a non-negligible fallback rate (15.6% in the office), and OOD collision rate does not improve consistently with model or data scale.

Evaluation is on proprietary data and robots with no public benchmark or standard baselines, so results are hard to reproduce or compare. Astra-Global also runs on the cloud, adding latency and connectivity dependence.
